details: 29 Oct, design review of the ALIX worktree-folder fix: outside that change. A relay lane started in ALIX would create an unignored .worktrees/ folder in its main checkout instead of using bin/wt. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
failing_case: A lane started for ALIX: worktree = os.path.join(main, ".worktrees", name). ALIX ignores only /.worktree/, so its main
checkout shows "?? .worktrees/", and bin/wt's deps link and alixbase config are skipped. Expected: the project's
folder (project.worktrees or derived) or its gate.wt.
pass_cases: 1. Project with project.worktrees = ".worktree": lane worktree at <main>/.worktree/<name>.

details: CONFIRMED by reading and a one-line Python check: os.path.join('/repo', '/srv/wts'.strip('/'), 'fx') -> /repo/srv/wts/fx. The guard's rule strips only a trailing slash; the change's comment calls its line "the guard's rule" but strip("/") also strips the leading one. relay_setup.gitignore_lines treats os.path.isabs(folder) as "outside the project" and adds no ignore line, so the folder made inside main is unignored.
Reachable: a person can set an absolute folder; setup's tests (test_setup.py, "/Users/x/wt") treat it as supported.
evidence: lib/relay_setup.py:638-641: folder ... strip("/") only for the emptiness test; isabs(folder) -> no ignore line
tests/test_setup.py:215: for n, outside in enumerate(("/Users/x/wt", "../wt")):
failing_case: kit.toml [project] worktrees = "/Users/x/wt" (a folder outside the project, which relay_setup.gitignore_lines supports and tests/test_setup.py tests).

Now: the worktree is made inside the main checkout, in a folder no .gitignore line covers (setup adds none for an outside folder), so the main checkout shows "?? Users/" - the same defect this change fixes for ALIX.
fix_hint: Strip only trailing slashes (rstrip("/")), keep the default for an empty value, and join: os.path.join(main, folder, name) already keeps an absolute folder absolute. Best done in the one shared helper of F2.
pass_cases: 1. kit.toml worktrees = "/abs/wts" (abs = a temp folder outside main): start("fx") -> worktree == "/abs/wts/fx", and <main>/abs does not exist.
2. kit.toml worktrees = ".worktree": worktree == <main>/.worktree/fx (the new test, unchanged).
4. no kit.toml, or no project.worktrees key: worktree == <main>/.worktrees/fx.
5. kit.toml worktrees = "../wts": worktree == normpath(<main>/../wts/fx), outside main.
reason: tests/test_lanes_state.py:419 covers absolute, trailing slash, empty, ../; fails at 589298bd.
findings.summary: an absolute project.worktrees ("/Users/x/wt") loses its leading slash, so the lane worktree lands inside the main checkout

details: CONFIRMED by reading. The brief's front decision (owner can reverse): "reuse the guard's reader, do not write a second one". Project Python rule (CLAUDE.local.md, Python): "A record that several programs read ... has one typed record and one parser, shared by all of them." The guard imports lib modules (relay_git, on master), so a lib helper is reachable from it; moving relay_setup and the guard onto it can be one step or a follow-up item, but lane start should not add a third copy. F1 is a live example of the drift.
Size: 20 minutes for the helper plus lanes; +15 to move setup and the guard onto it.
evidence: git grep -n 'project.worktrees\|"worktrees"' -- lib plugins/relay/hooks: guard_main.py:230-234, relay_setup.py:637-638, relay_lanes.py:487-488
brief: "reuse the guard's reader, do not write a second one"
failing_case: git grep for the worktrees-folder default finds three rules for one kit.toml key:
plugins/relay/hooks/guard_main.py:231 (keeps a leading slash, strips one trailing slash, "" when the value is "/"),
lib/relay_setup.py:638 (keeps the value as written, isabs -> outside),
lib/relay_lanes.py:488 (new: strips all leading and trailing slashes).
For worktrees = "/Users/x/wt" the three give: guard <main>//Users/x/wt, setup "outside the project", lanes <main>/Users/x/wt.
Expected: one helper (e.g. relay_config.worktrees_folder(main) -> absolute folder) that lane start uses, so the lane, the gitignore line and the guard agree.
fix_hint: Add relay_config.worktrees_folder(main: str) -> str (reads load_bindings, rstrip("/"), default ".worktrees", returns os.path.join(main, value)); call it in relay_lanes.start. Optionally switch relay_setup.gitignore_lines and Guard.setup to it.
pass_cases: 1. relay_lanes.start computes its folder by calling one shared function (no inline isinstance/strip rule left in relay_lanes.py); git grep '"\.worktrees"' in lib/relay_lanes.py finds nothing.
2. That function: no kit.toml -> <main>/.worktrees; ".worktree" -> <main>/.worktree; ".worktree/" -> <main>/.worktree; "/abs/wts" -> /abs/wts; "" or a non-string -> <main>/.worktrees.

findings.summary: a third copy of the project.worktrees rule, against the brief's "reuse the guard's reader" and the one-parser rule; the copies already disagree

details: CONFIRMED by running the functions. Outside the change (relay_estimate.py, queue_ext/estimate.py untouched), but this change makes it reachable for relay's own lanes: before it, an ALIX lane still sat in .worktrees/ and was counted. The regexes WORKTREE and WORKTREE_PATH and repo_top hardcode ".worktrees". A queue item, not a fix here.
failing_case: An agent of an ALIX lane works in /x/alix/.worktree/fx/lib, or its brief says "Worktree: /x/alix/.worktree/fx (branch wt/fx)".

Now: relay_estimate.worktree_of('/x/alix/.worktree/fx/lib') -> None; change_of('/x/alix', 'Worktree: /x/alix/.worktree/fx (branch wt/fx)') -> None; queue_ext/estimate.repo_top keeps the worktree as the repo.
fix_hint: Take the project's worktrees folder (F2's helper) where the root is known, or match git's worktree list; keep ".worktrees" as the fallback when no root is given.
reason: Outside the change, owner queue item; fixer agrees.
findings.summary: cost attribution finds a change only under .worktrees/, so lane agents in a .worktree project (ALIX) count for no change
